title: Nestorius and Cyril on the Title of Mary
english: Nestorius says: When the divine Scripture speaks of the birth of Christ from Mary the virgin, it nowhere appears as God, but as Christ or the Lord Jesus, because these three terms are significant of the two natures, now referring to one, now to the other; I mean: When the birth from the Virgin is announced to us of Christ, the Apostle says, 'God sent his Son, born of a woman'; he did not say, 'Sent God the Word'; but he takes the name indicating the two births, namely God and man, because Christ is double; for the Virgin bore a Son of God, as he breathed; but you are gods and sons of the Most High all, whence we learned to say Christotokos, Kyriotokos, anthropotokos from Scripture, but we were never taught to call the holy virgin Theotokos, that is, God-bearer or Mother of God.
Cyril says: Isaiah cries in the Spirit saying: 'Behold the virgin shall conceive in womb and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel' (Isaiah 7:14), which is.
